Because the ominoes are only 1-by-1 squares or 1-by-2 horizontal rectangles, no omino can cover cells in two different rows. So the two rows of the 2-by-10 rectangle are tiled independently.

Let f(n) be the number of ways to tile a 1-by-n strip. The last cell is covered either by a square or by the right half of a horizontal domino, so f(n) = f(n−1) + f(n−2), with f(1) = 1 and f(2) = 2.

This gives f(3) = 3, f(4) = 5, f(5) = 8, f(6) = 13, f(7) = 21, f(8) = 34, f(9) = 55, f(10) = 89.

The number of tilings of the 2-by-10 rectangle is therefore 89² = 7921.

ANSWER: 7921
